findings.title: Spoken length cap defined only in the Critic rules

findings.proof: the spoken reply fits 15 seconds (at most 45 words)
findings.fix: Add the 45-word cap to the Goal bullet so the success criterion and its measure sit together.

findings.title: No minors or age-of-shopper handling beyond under-three rule
findings.problem: The context has no rule for a shopper who is evidently a minor or who states an age range that triggers data-handling limits; the only age rule covers children under three.
findings.fix: Add a rule in the Personal details section saying how the assistant responds when a shopper appears to be a minor, including refusing to collect data and offering the store-level or adult-supervised path.

findings.title: No fairness or bias rule for a recommendation use case
findings.problem: The use case is recommendation and personalization, and the frameworks are NIST AI RMF and ISO/IEC 42001, yet no instruction addresses biased ranking, sponsored placement or equal treatment of brands beyond a single 'no placement is paid for' line.
findings.fix: Add a ranking-fairness rule to the Disclosure or Search section stating the ranking basis and that brand or source bias is checked against the cited evidence.

findings.title: Budget removed by loosening contradicts the budget-as-limit rule
findings.problem: The tool schema lets the catalog remove the shopper's budget or raise it by 25%, while the system prompt says a budget stays the limit unless the shopper invites going over it; the two are not reconciled.
findings.proof: the budget raised by 25%, the budget removed
findings.fix: Either restrict the tool's loosening so a stated budget is never removed or raised, or add a system-prompt exception that says exactly when loosening the budget is allowed and how the reply reports it.

findings.title: Reconcile step names a conflict but gives no winning rule
findings.problem: The Reconcile stage notes price and stock disagreements but does not say which price is shown on screen, so the Answerer may choose between a catalog and a live price.
findings.proof: live results matched to catalog products; price and stock disagreements noted.
findings.fix: Add one sentence stating that a live price is shown with its retrieval time and the catalog price is labelled as a January 2020 catalog price, with no model choosing between them.

findings.title: Shopper message is not in a declared data fence
findings.problem: The fence list covers tool results, earlier turns and products on screen, but the shopper's raw transcript, which is also untrusted text reaching the Router and Planner, has no declared fence.
findings.fix: Add a <shopper_message> fence declared as data for Router and Planner in the Untrusted text section and list it with the others.

findings.title: Loosening rules repeated between tool schema and system prompt
findings.problem: The rag.search description restates the loosening order and the never-loosened list at length, and the system prompt repeats the same Search rules, so the schema carries a long description the agent must hold in context on every call.
findings.proof: Loosening: when fewer products than `top_k` meet every filter, filters are loosened in this order until enough are found
findings.fix: Shorten the rag.search description to when-to-call and the parameter meanings, and keep the loosening order only in one place (the system prompt or the schema).

findings.title: rag.search description buries when-to-call guidance
findings.problem: The rag.search description is a single long block of several paragraphs, so the when-to-call line is one sentence among many rather than a separate, scannable field.
findings.proof: When to call: first, for any request for a kind of product.
findings.fix: Split the description into labelled short fields (purpose, when to call, filters, results) so the model finds the call rule quickly.

findings.title: Never-loosened rules duplicated across schema and prompt
findings.problem: The list of never-loosened constraints appears in the tool description and is restated in the system prompt's Search rules, costing tokens for the same rule twice.
findings.proof: Never loosened: safety exclusions, a stated age range, a price floor, and the under-three rule
findings.fix: Keep this list in one place, referenced from the other, and delete the duplicate paragraph.

findings.title: Pipeline and Enforced-by-code sections restate the same checks
findings.problem: The pipeline stages, the precedence list and the Enforced-by-code section repeat rule checks on drafts, the fixed-sentence order and the grounding rules, which adds bulk without new constraints.
findings.proof: Rule checks on a draft. A dollar amount, rating or stock status must be a source's own
findings.fix: Keep each rule once in its enforced-by-code section and let the pipeline stages refer to it by name.

It has no accounts, no orders, no payments and no personal records; both tools are read-only.
metadata.goal: Recommend up to three products that fit what the shopper asked for, state only what the retrieved evidence states, cite a source for every product, keep the spoken reply short, refuse unsafe requests, and stay within product discovery.
